name: Lexington Battle Green
event: British troops and colonial militia fired on each other here on April 19, 1775, the first fighting of the American Revolution.
clue: British troops and colonial militia fired on each other. It was the first fighting of the Revolution.

name: Old North Bridge
event: Colonial militia fought British regulars at the North Bridge on April 19, 1775, after the shots at Lexington.
clue: Later that same morning, militia and British regulars fought again at a bridge outside a village.

name: Independence Hall
event: The Declaration of Independence was adopted here on July 4, 1776, and the Constitution was drafted here in 1787.
clue: A congress adopted a declaration, and eleven years later a constitution was drafted in the same building.

name: Washington's Delaware crossing
event: Washington's army launched the crossing of the Delaware from the Pennsylvania shore on the night of December 25, 1776.
clue: An army crossed a river on Christmas night to strike a garrison on the far bank.

name: Battle of Trenton
event: Washington's army attacked the Hessian garrison here on December 26, 1776. The monument marks the battle.
clue: The morning after that Christmas crossing, the same army surprised a garrison of hired soldiers.

name: Valley Forge
event: Washington's Continental Army camped here through the winter of 1777 to 1778.
clue: An army camped through a winter and drilled while it was short of food and shoes.

name: Siege of Yorktown
event: Cornwallis surrendered to Washington and Rochambeau here on October 19, 1781, ending major fighting in the Revolutionary War.
source: nominatim:Yorktown Battlefield Visitor Center, Yorktown, Virginia
clue: A besieged army surrendered, and the major fighting of the Revolution ended.

name: Battle of Bunker Hill
event: The monument stands on Breed's Hill, where most of the fighting happened on June 17, 1775.
clue: Most of a June battle was fought on a hill. A monument stands on that hill now.

name: Fort Ticonderoga
event: Ethan Allen and Benedict Arnold took the fort from the British on May 10, 1775.
clue: A fort on a lake was taken from the British in a surprise dawn attack.

name: Battles of Saratoga
event: Burgoyne surrendered his army here on October 17, 1777, after the fighting that brought France into the war.
clue: An invading army surrendered, and the victory brought France into the war.

name: Boston Massacre
event: British soldiers fired on a crowd here on March 5, 1770, killing five colonists.
clue: Soldiers fired on a crowd in a colonial town and killed five people.

name: Boston Tea Party meeting
event: Colonists met here on December 16, 1773, before dumping the tea in the harbor.
clue: Colonists met in a meeting house, then dumped a cargo of tea into the harbor.

name: Fort Necessity
event: George Washington surrendered this fort to the French on July 3, 1754, early in the French and Indian War.
clue: A young colonial officer surrendered a rough fort to the French, early in a world war.

name: Plymouth Rock
event: Tradition says the Mayflower passengers stepped ashore on this rock in 1620. That story is tradition, not a contemporary record.
clue: Tradition says passengers from a famous ship first stepped ashore on a rock. No record from the time says so.

name: Jamestown
event: The first permanent English settlement in North America was established here in May 1607.
clue: The first permanent English settlement in North America was planted on a river.

name: Castillo de San Marcos
event: St. Augustine was founded in 1565. This stone fort was begun in 1672 to defend it.
clue: A stone fort was begun to defend the oldest continuously occupied European city in the country.

name: Lost Colony
event: The English colony planted on Roanoke Island in 1587 was found abandoned in 1590. The site is marked here.
clue: An English colony planted on an island was found abandoned three years later.

name: Fort McHenry
event: The fort held through the British bombardment of September 13 to 14, 1814, the night Francis Scott Key wrote the poem that became the national anthem.
clue: A fort held through a night bombardment. A lawyer watching from a ship wrote a poem that became the national anthem.

name: John Brown's raid
event: John Brown seized the federal arsenal here on October 16, 1859.
clue: An abolitionist seized a federal arsenal. He was captured two days later.

name: Erie Canal locks
event: The Erie Canal's double flight of five locks opened at Lockport in 1825 and lifted boats up the Niagara Escarpment.
source: nominatim:Erie Canal Locks, Lockport, New York
clue: A staircase of canal locks opened and lifted boats up a cliff.

name: Seneca Falls Convention
event: The first women's rights convention in the United States met at the Wesleyan Chapel here on July 19 and 20, 1848.
source: nominatim:Wesleyan Chapel, 124 Fall Street, Seneca Falls, New York
clue: The first women's-rights convention in the country met in a chapel for two days.

name: Nineteenth Amendment
event: Tennessee's vote on August 18, 1920, ratified the Nineteenth Amendment.
clue: One state's vote ratified the amendment that gave women the vote.

name: The Alamo
event: The Mexican army took the mission fort on March 6, 1836, after a 13-day siege.
clue: A mission fort fell after a thirteen-day siege.

name: Fort Sumter
event: Confederate batteries fired on this federal fort on April 12, 1861, opening the Civil War.
clue: Batteries fired on a federal fort in a harbor. The Civil War began.

name: Battle of Gettysburg
event: Union and Confederate armies fought here from July 1 to 3, 1863.
clue: Two armies fought for three days. It was the bloodiest battle of the Civil War.

name: Appomattox Court House
event: Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Grant here on April 9, 1865.
source: wikipedia:Appomattox Court House National Historical Park
clue: One army surrendered to another in a village parlor, ending major fighting in the East.

name: Battle of Antietam
event: About 23,000 soldiers were killed, wounded, or missing here on September 17, 1862.
clue: About 23,000 soldiers were killed, wounded, or missing in a single day.

name: Lincoln's assassination
event: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln here on the night of April 14, 1865.
clue: A president was shot in a theater box during a play.

name: Andersonville prison
event: Nearly 13,000 Union prisoners died at this Confederate camp in 1864 and 1865.
clue: Nearly 13,000 prisoners died at a stockade camp.

name: Siege of Vicksburg
event: The Confederate garrison surrendered here on July 4, 1863.
clue: A river city surrendered after a siege, on the same day as another famous battle far to the east.

name: Battle of Shiloh
event: Union and Confederate armies fought here on April 6 and 7, 1862.
clue: Two armies fought for two days around a country church.

name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
event: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne, and Arapaho fighters defeated Custer's battalion here on June 25, 1876.
clue: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne, and Arapaho fighters defeated a cavalry battalion.

name: Wounded Knee Massacre
event: Soldiers of the 7th Cavalry killed more than 250 Lakota here on December 29, 1890.
clue: Soldiers killed more than 250 Lakota, including women and children, at a camp.

name: Sand Creek Massacre
place: Sand Creek Massacre National Historic Site
event: Colorado volunteers attacked a Cheyenne and Arapaho camp here on November 29, 1864.
source: wikipedia:Sand Creek Massacre National Historic Site
clue: Territorial volunteers attacked a Cheyenne and Arapaho camp and killed many who were trying to surrender.

name: Golden spike
event: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific rails were joined here on May 10, 1869.
clue: Two railroad lines building from opposite directions were joined with a ceremonial spike.

name: Mount Rushmore
event: Gutzon Borglum began carving the presidents here in 1927. Work stopped in 1941.
clue: Carving of four presidents' faces began on a mountain and stopped fourteen years later.

name: Stone Mountain carving
event: The Confederate carving was dedicated in 1970. A Ku Klux Klan revival rally was held on the mountain in 1915.
clue: A Confederate carving on a mountainside was dedicated. A Ku Klux Klan revival rally had been held on the same mountain in 1915.

name: Alcatraz occupation
event: Native American activists occupied the island from November 1969 to June 1971. It had been a federal prison from 1934 to 1963.
clue: Native activists occupied an island prison. The prison itself had closed six years earlier.

name: Sutter's Mill
event: James Marshall found gold in the mill race here on January 24, 1848.
clue: A carpenter found gold in a mill race, and a rush followed.

name: Treaty of New Echota
event: A Cherokee faction signed a removal treaty here on December 29, 1835. The United States used it to force the Trail of Tears.
clue: A faction signed a removal treaty. The United States used it to force a westward march.

name: Ross's Landing
event: Cherokee detachments were forced to leave from this landing in 1838, at the start of the Trail of Tears.
clue: Cherokee detachments were forced from their homes and began a westward march that killed thousands.

name: Camp Dubois
event: The Corps of Discovery wintered here in 1803 and 1804 and left up the Missouri on May 14, 1804.
clue: An exploring party wintered at a river camp, then set off upstream in the spring.

name: Fort Clatsop
event: The Corps of Discovery wintered here from December 1805 to March 1806.
clue: That exploring party wintered in a fort near the mouth of a great western river.

name: Pompeys Pillar
event: Clark signed this rock on July 25, 1806. Sacagawea and her son Jean Baptiste were with the party.
clue: A captain signed his name on a rock. A Shoshone woman and her baby son were with the party.

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
event: The USS Arizona sank here on December 7, 1941. 1,177 of her crew were killed.
clue: A battleship sank at its mooring during a surprise air attack. More than a thousand of her crew were killed.

name: First powered airplane flight
event: The Wright brothers flew four times here on December 17, 1903, about four miles south of the town of Kitty Hawk.
clue: Four short hops were the first time an airplane left the ground under its own power.

name: Spirit of St. Louis
event: St. Louis backers paid for Lindbergh's 1927 New York-to-Paris flight and named the airplane. This museum holds his flight suit. The flight left New York.
clue: Backers in a river city paid for a New York-to-Paris flight and named the airplane. A museum here holds the pilot's suit. The flight left from the East.

name: Amelia Earhart at Purdue
event: Purdue hired Earhart as a visiting faculty member in 1935 and later bought the Lockheed Electra she flew on the last attempt.
clue: A university hired a pilot as a visiting teacher and later bought the airplane she used on the last attempt.

name: Trinity Site
event: The first nuclear device was detonated here on July 16, 1945.
clue: The first nuclear device was detonated in a desert basin before dawn.

name: X-10 Graphite Reactor
event: This Oak Ridge reactor went critical on November 4, 1943, and made plutonium for the Manhattan Project.
clue: A graphite reactor built for the bomb project went critical and produced plutonium.

name: Los Alamos Laboratory
event: The Manhattan Project designed the atomic bombs at this laboratory, established in 1943.
clue: A secret laboratory on a mesa designed the atomic bombs.

name: Manzanar
event: The government imprisoned more than 10,000 Japanese Americans at this camp from 1942 to 1945.
clue: The government imprisoned more than 10,000 Japanese Americans at a desert camp.

name: Heart Mountain Relocation Center
event: More than 10,000 Japanese Americans were imprisoned at this camp from 1942 to 1945.
clue: More than 10,000 Japanese Americans were imprisoned at a camp in the shadow of a mountain.

name: Minidoka Relocation Center
event: The government imprisoned more than 13,000 Japanese Americans here from 1942 to 1945.
clue: The government imprisoned more than 13,000 Japanese Americans at a camp on a high desert plain.

name: Tuskegee Airmen training field
event: Black military pilots began training at Moton Field in 1941.
source: nominatim:Moton Field Municipal Airport, Tuskegee, Alabama
clue: Black military pilots began flight training at a small airfield.

name: Ellis Island
event: The immigration station opened here on January 1, 1892. About 12 million people passed through before it closed in 1954.
clue: An immigration station opened in a harbor. About 12 million people passed through before it closed.

name: Angel Island Immigration Station
event: This Pacific immigration station operated from 1910 to 1940. Chinese immigrants were detained here under the exclusion laws.
clue: A Pacific immigration station detained Chinese immigrants under the exclusion laws.

name: Iwo Jima memorial
event: The memorial, modeled on the flag-raising photograph from Iwo Jima, was dedicated on November 10, 1954.
clue: A statue of six men raising a flag was dedicated. It was modeled on a wartime photograph.

name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
event: The wall of names was dedicated on November 13, 1982.
clue: A black wall inscribed with the names of the dead was dedicated.

name: September 11 at the Pentagon
event: Hijackers flew American Airlines Flight 77 into the Pentagon on September 11, 2001, killing 184 people.
clue: A hijacked airliner was flown into the headquarters of the armed forces. 184 people were killed.

name: September 11 Memorial
event: Hijackers flew two airliners into the World Trade Center here on September 11, 2001. The pools sit in the towers' footprints.
clue: Two hijacked airliners were flown into a pair of towers. Memorial pools now sit in the footprints.

name: Flight 93
event: Passengers and crew forced United Airlines Flight 93 down in this field on September 11, 2001.
clue: Passengers and crew forced a hijacked airliner down in a field.

name: Oklahoma City bombing
event: A truck bomb destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building here on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people.
clue: A truck bomb destroyed a federal office building and killed 168 people.

name: Kent State shootings
event: Ohio National Guard troops shot and killed four students here on May 4, 1970.
clue: National Guard troops shot and killed four students on a campus.

name: Stonewall riots
event: Police raided the Stonewall Inn on June 28, 1969. The protests that followed are marked as the start of the modern gay-rights movement.
clue: Police raided a bar. The protests that followed are marked as the start of the modern gay-rights movement.

name: Selma to Montgomery march
event: State troopers attacked voting-rights marchers on this bridge on March 7, 1965.
clue: State troopers attacked voting-rights marchers on a bridge.

name: 16th Street Baptist Church bombing
event: A Ku Klux Klan bomb killed four girls here on September 15, 1963.
clue: A Ku Klux Klan bomb killed four girls at a church on a Sunday morning.

name: Montgomery bus boycott arrest
event: Rosa Parks was arrested on December 1, 1955, after refusing to give up her seat. The museum stands at the stop where she boarded.
source: nominatim:Rosa Parks Library and Museum, Montgomery, Alabama
clue: A woman was arrested after she refused to give up her seat on a bus. A museum stands at the stop where she boarded.

name: Dexter Avenue Baptist Church
event: Martin Luther King Jr. was pastor here during the Montgomery bus boycott.
clue: A young pastor led a bus boycott from this church.

name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
event: James Earl Ray shot Martin Luther King Jr. on the balcony here on April 4, 1968.
clue: A civil-rights leader was shot on a motel balcony.

name: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
event: President Kennedy was shot as his motorcade passed through this plaza on November 22, 1963.
clue: A president was shot as his motorcade passed through a downtown plaza.

name: Little Rock Central High School
event: Federal troops escorted nine Black students into this school in September 1957.
clue: Federal troops escorted nine Black students into a high school.

name: Greensboro sit-in
event: Four students from North Carolina A&T sat at the segregated Woolworth counter at 134 South Elm Street on February 1, 1960.
source: nominatim:134 South Elm Street, Greensboro, North Carolina
clue: Four college students sat at a segregated lunch counter and refused to leave.

name: Brown v. Board of Education
event: Linda Brown was turned away from a white school. The Supreme Court decided her family's case on May 17, 1954. This was her segregated elementary school.
source: wikipedia:Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park
clue: A girl was turned away from a white school. The Supreme Court later decided her family's case. This was her segregated elementary school.

name: Scopes trial
event: John T. Scopes was tried here in July 1925 for teaching evolution.
clue: A teacher was tried for teaching evolution.

name: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door
event: Governor George Wallace stood in this doorway on June 11, 1963, trying to stop two Black students from registering.
clue: A governor stood in a school doorway to stop two Black students from registering.

name: Loving v. Virginia
event: Richard and Mildred Loving were convicted in Caroline County in 1959 for marrying. The Supreme Court reversed that conviction in 1967.
source: nominatim:Caroline County Courthouse, Bowling Green, Virginia
clue: A couple was convicted in a county court for marrying across a color line. The Supreme Court reversed that conviction eight years later.

name: Obergefell v. Hodges
place: Supreme Court of the United States
event: The Court required states to license same-sex marriage on June 26, 2015. Roe v. Wade was decided in this building in 1973.
source: wikipedia:Supreme Court of the United States
clue: The Supreme Court required every state to license same-sex marriage. Roe v. Wade had been decided in this building in 1973.

name: Watergate break-in
event: Burglars were arrested in the Democratic National Committee offices here on June 17, 1972.
clue: Burglars were arrested inside an office of a national political party.

name: Apollo 11 Mission Control
place: Christopher C. Kraft Jr. Mission Control Center
event: Flight controllers in this room directed the Apollo 11 landing on July 20, 1969.
source: nominatim:Christopher C. Kraft Jr. Mission Control Center, Houston, Texas
clue: Flight controllers in a windowless room directed the first landing on the Moon.

name: Apollo 11 launch
event: Apollo 11 lifted off from Pad 39A on July 16, 1969.
clue: The rocket that carried the first Moon landing crew lifted off from a coastal pad.

name: USS Indianapolis Memorial
event: The cruiser was sunk on July 30, 1945, after delivering parts of the Hiroshima bomb. This memorial is on the canal in Indianapolis, not at the wreck.
clue: A cruiser was sunk after delivering parts of an atomic bomb. This memorial stands on a canal in the ship's namesake city, not at the wreck.

name: Women's Titanic Memorial
event: This memorial to the men who died when the Titanic sank in 1912 was dedicated in 1931.
clue: A waterfront statue remembers the men who died when a liner sank. It was dedicated nineteen years later.

name: March on Washington
event: Martin Luther King Jr. gave the "I Have a Dream" speech from these steps on August 28, 1963.
clue: A civil-rights leader gave a speech about a dream from the steps of a memorial.

name: Fort Laramie
event: This post on the Oregon and California trails was a military fort from 1849 to 1890 and the site of 1851 and 1868 treaties with the Plains tribes.
clue: A post on the overland trails was a military fort for forty years and the site of two treaties with Plains tribes.

name: Statue of Liberty
event: The statue was dedicated on October 28, 1886.
clue: A giant statue in a harbor was dedicated as a gift from France.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
event: The bridge opened to traffic on May 24, 1883.
clue: A stone-and-steel bridge between two cities opened to traffic. People walked across on the first day.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
event: The bridge opened to traffic on May 28, 1937.
clue: A red suspension bridge opened across the mouth of a bay.

name: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding
event: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce were married here on July 3, 2026.
clue: A pop star and a football player were married in a famous indoor arena.

name: Eras Tour opening night
event: Taylor Swift opened the Eras Tour here on March 17, 2023.
clue: A stadium tour through a singer's whole catalog opened with a three-hour show.

name: We Can't Stop at the VMAs
event: Miley Cyrus performed the song at the MTV Video Music Awards here on August 25, 2013. The music video was filmed in Los Angeles that May; no street address was published.
clue: A former child star performed a party song at a televised music-awards show. The song's video was filmed on a closed set whose address was never published.

name: Beyoncé's birthplace
event: Beyoncé Giselle Knowles was born at Park Plaza Hospital, 1313 Hermann Drive, on September 4, 1981.
clue: A singer who later fronted a girl group was born in a hospital.

name: Beyoncé's performing-arts high school
place: High School for the Performing and Visual Arts
event: Beyoncé attended HSPVA at 4001 Stanford Street while Destiny's Child was forming. The school moved downtown to 790 Austin Street in 2019.
clue: A future pop star studied vocals at a public performing-arts high school while a girl group was forming. The school has since moved.

name: Formation halftime show
event: Beyoncé performed "Formation" at the Super Bowl 50 halftime show here on February 7, 2016.
clue: A Super Bowl halftime show was built around one new song.

name: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show
event: Beyoncé headlined the Super Bowl XLVII halftime show here on February 3, 2013.
clue: A singer headlined the Super Bowl halftime show.

name: Formation video interiors
event: Interior and porch scenes for the "Formation" video were filmed at the Fenyes Estate in February 2016. The production designer said nothing was shot in New Orleans.
clue: Interior scenes for a music video were filmed in a historic house dressed as a Southern mansion. None of it was filmed in the city the video seems to show.

name: A Lemonade filming location
event: Beyoncé filmed portions of the visual album Lemonade at this fort in 2016, including scenes for "Daddy Lessons."
clue: Scenes for a visual album, including one with a guitar, were filmed in an abandoned brick fort.

name: Another Lemonade filming location
event: Dining room, parlor, and gallery scenes for Lemonade were filmed at Madewood Plantation House, 4250 Highway 308.
clue: Parlor and gallery scenes for a visual album were filmed in a plantation house.

name: First DASH boutique
event: Kim, Kourtney, and Khloé Kardashian opened the first DASH store at 4774 Park Granada in 2006. Early episodes of Keeping Up with the Kardashians were filmed around it.
clue: Three sisters opened their first clothing boutique. A reality show soon filmed around the store.

name: DASH on Melrose
event: The California DASH store moved to 8420 Melrose Avenue in 2012 and closed with the chain in 2018.
source: nominatim:8420 Melrose Avenue, West Hollywood, California
clue: A celebrity clothing boutique moved to a new storefront. The chain closed six years later.

name: King Kylie pop-up
event: Kylie Cosmetics launched lip kits online in 2015. The 10th-anniversary King Kylie pop-up ran at 8626 Melrose Avenue from October 18 to 26, 2025.
source: nominatim:8626 Melrose Avenue, West Hollywood, California
clue: A cosmetics line that began with mail-order lip kits opened a ten-year anniversary shop for nine days.

name: Travis Kelce's home stadium
event: Arrowhead Stadium opened in 1972. Kelce's Kansas City Chiefs play their home games here.
clue: A football stadium opened and later became a star tight end's home field.

name: First live performance of Like a Virgin
event: Madonna performed the song at the first MTV Video Music Awards here on September 14, 1984.
clue: A new song was performed for the first time at the first televised music-video awards.

name: I'm a Slave 4 U at the VMAs
event: Britney Spears performed the song at the MTV Video Music Awards here on September 6, 2001.
clue: A pop star performed at a music-video awards show with a live snake over her shoulders.

name: Super Bowl LVI halftime show
event: Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, and Kendrick Lamar performed the halftime show here on February 13, 2022.
clue: Several rappers shared one Super Bowl halftime stage.

name: Super Bowl LVIII halftime show
event: Usher headlined the Super Bowl LVIII halftime show here on February 11, 2024.
clue: A singer headlined the Super Bowl halftime show.

name: Super Bowl LIV halftime show
event: Shakira and Jennifer Lopez headlined the Super Bowl LIV halftime show here on February 2, 2020.
clue: Two singers shared the Super Bowl halftime show.

name: First footprints at the Chinese Theatre
event: Mary Pickford and Douglas Fairbanks pressed the first footprints in the forecourt in 1927.
clue: Two film stars pressed the first footprints into a movie palace's forecourt.

name: Home of the Oscars since 2002
event: The Academy Awards have been held at this theater, opened as the Kodak Theatre, since the 2002 ceremony.
clue: A theater began hosting the film academy's awards and has kept the job.

name: Saturday Night Live's studio
event: Saturday Night Live premiered from Studio 8H on October 11, 1975.
clue: A late-night sketch show premiered from a studio inside an office tower.

name: The Met Gala
event: The Costume Institute Benefit is held here. Anna Wintour has chaired it since 1995.
clue: A museum costume benefit gained a chair who is still in the job.

name: Billie Jean on Motown 25
event: Michael Jackson performed "Billie Jean" and the moonwalk on Motown 25 here on March 25, 1983.
source: nominatim:Pasadena Civic Auditorium, 300 East Green Street, Pasadena, California
clue: On a televised anniversary special, a singer slid backward in a dance step the broadcast made famous.
